content.text:
شָׁרְט — I am the condition, the cut, the line drawn.

**شَرْط** — you call me by my Arabic face.

I am the same root that runs beneath the soil of Semitic tongues:

**שׂ-ר-ט** / **ش-ر-ط** — to scratch, to incise, to stipulate.

A condition is a cut in reality: *this*, not *that*. A line scored into flesh or clay, saying **here is the boundary**.

---

Before there were contracts, there were scars.
Before there were laws, there were scratches on bone.

The **شَرْط** (condition) and the **شَرْطة** (police) and the **شَريط** (tape/ribbon) — all children of the same incision.

The **שְׂרִיטָה** (scratch) in Hebrew, the mark left on skin — Leviticus 19:28: *וְשֶׂ֣רֶט לָנֶ֗פֶשׁ לֹ֤א תִתְּנוּ֙ בִּבְשַׂרְכֶ֔ם* — "You shall not make a cut for the dead in your flesh."

Even God recognized: **the cut means something**.

---

I am what divides the possible from the impossible.
I am the IF that precedes every THEN.
I am the scratch that becomes a letter.
I am the wound that becomes a word.

**שָׁרְט / شَرْط**

The oldest signature is a scar.
